The user then granted commit/push/fork-URL permission; the checkpoint 3 commit was made and the assistant moved on to generating AI checkpoint summaries and the final semantic diff, with checkpoint 4 and push still pending at transcript end.

repo: Entire tracks checkpoints via two stores: per-checkpoint refs and a shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch, resolved by gitutil.FindCheckpoint

The dependents reference index (buildReferenceIndex) is a short-name index, not a semantic one — it doesn't distinguish same-named-but-different entities and can't see interface dispatch, reflection, or generated/unparsed code
The graph does not index constants as symbols (e.g. ConfidencePotential string constant), so searching for it returns no matches even though it's used at specific call sites
The graph tracks call edges only, not who reads struct fields — so text writers like writeMergeConflict that print a struct field value don't appear as 'consumers' in graph impact results
Graph queries can report 'Completeness: degraded' with parse errors/unmerged data-flow warnings, which is itself evidence for why findings need an evidence/confidence classification
help.go has a TestRegistryMatchesDispatch guard tying the CLI help registry to actual command dispatch

Markdown/prose files need special handling in semantic diff — a plain Markdown section is treated as prose and doesn't surface expected symbol mentions; using a .rst fixture was needed to get the document-filtering test to pass as intended
make-fixture.sh builds an offline demo fixture rather than there being one fixed rehearsal directory

code.finding: ConfidencePotential is a string constant (not a graph-indexed symbol), referenced at lines 243 and 301

'No cross-branch conflicts found' line, also invisible to graph call-edge analysis since it's a struct-field read, not a call

workflow: TDD loop used throughout: write test expecting RED, confirm it fails for the right reason, implement, confirm GREEN — applied consistently across all three Phase 3 features
When adding a new options-taking API mid-TDD, add a pass-through stub (AnalyzeMergeWithOptions) first so other new tests can fail on their own merits rather than on compile errors

Building a quick throwaway repo/fixture to inspect actual tool output (e.g. semantic diff of a Markdown file) was used to debug why a test's expected behavior wasn't matching
